text:
maya: opened PR #8310 - allocator tweak landed in feature branch. quick perf smoke shows a noticeable p95 bump on long sequences and a small RSS increase, tagging for quick eyes

maya: bench command i ran: `./infra/bench/run_longseq.sh --model rwd-v2 --seq 8192 --runs 6`

maya: paste of the relevant output:
```
run 1: p50=118ms p95=322ms p99=612ms rss=2.06GB
run 2: p50=121ms p95=335ms p99=630ms rss=2.11GB
baseline median p95 (main): 290ms, baseline rss: 1.98GB
```

maya: so p95 ~+15% and rss +120MB. i didn't see errors, but canary not yet deployed. please request reviewers / quick thumbs if we should hold merge.

sam: pinged on PR. can you post the commit sha and the artifact link?

maya: sha=abc123def4, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8310, bench artifact: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/8310/longseq/bench.csv

taylor: will run a local replicate in a few mins. do we know whether this shows up with small batches too? or only larger aggregate throughput?

maya: observed even with single-client runs; more pronounced under concurrent load. single request p95 is slightly up.

frank: quick skim of the change — allocator path removed a short-circuit that avoided mutex in the small-batch hot path. that could add contention for certain thread counts.

lina: tagging @sam @frank as reviewers. we need 2 approvals and a green canary before merging per policy.

sam: reproducing now. running `bench_longseq --parallel 8 --runs 3` locally. i'll dump lock histograms if i see contention.

ci-bot: canary job queued: canary-8310 -> staging-north. Tests: longseq-smoke, mem-smoke, basic-e2e. ETA ~12m.

maya: thanks. FYI i added a small debug flag in the branch: `ALLOC_DEBUG=1` to emit allocator histograms to logs when enabled.

taylor: local run complete: p95 delta only shows up when `batch_size >= 16` or concurrency > 4. attached truncated logs: `p95=318ms` at batch 32 vs baseline `p95=276ms`.

frank: can you try toggling the fast-path back on (introduce a config guard) and re-run? if that fixes it we can ship with flag defaulting to old behavior and iterate.

maya: ok i'll open a small follow-up PR that gates the new path behind `--enable-new-alloc`. planning to request quick merge of that as a revert-style guard so we don't block other work.

sam: fine with that. if canary passes + the opt-in default is off, i'm +1 to merge the allocator change behind the flag later after more perf tuning.

lina: agree with sampler. hold merge for canary results right now. please post canary job link and final verdict.

ci-bot: canary-8310 finished: longseq-smoke=FAILED (p95 above threshold), mem-smoke=PASS, basic-e2e=PASS. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/8310/canary-results.json

maya: ack. i'll not merge. opening opt-in flag PR now. ETA ~40m. anyone want to help iterate on lock elimination?

taylor: i'll take a look at the allocator flamegraph after your next run.

frank: i'll instrument the mutex hotspots and try a patch that reduces contention.

sam: once the opt-in flag PR is up, i'll run the same canary flow and re-check p95.

lina: thanks all — good async coordination. mark `hold` on PR until opt-in PR + passing canary. :lock:
